fixtures.preview: A Sunday 2pm Roses clash at Elland Road, with Michael Carrick's United looking for a response after a 2-0 loss at Atlético Madrid.
talking_points: United lost 2-0 at Atlético on Tuesday night (Europe time), their fourth defeat of the season, and have won just one of their last seven games.
Leny Yoro was sent off in Madrid; whether it affects this league game isn't confirmed (UEFA bans normally apply to the next European match).
Before the Atlético game, Dorgu, Sesko, de Ligt and Ugarte were reported out and Mazraoui was 'not quite right'; fresh injury news is still to come.
Leeds ended a five-game unbeaten league start with a 2-1 loss at Arsenal, and are without Dan James and Joe Rodon, with Harry Wilson and Bahoya back in training.

fixtures.preview: A trip to Lake Como for matchday 3 of the Champions League league phase, with United on one win and one defeat.
A Sunday home game against Bournemouth, moved from Saturday for UK TV.
A lunchtime trip to Stamford Bridge, moved to a 12:30pm UK start for TV.
Matchday 4 of the Champions League league phase brings Roma to Old Trafford.
The A-League Men season opens with a Friday-night Sydney Derby, with former Sydney FC coach Ufuk Talay now in charge of the Wanderers.
talking_points: Talay, who left Sydney FC in March, returns to Allianz Stadium as Wanderers coach and says he is focused on his players, not the reception.
Coach Patrick Kisnorbo says his side has had sixteen weeks to prepare, and captain Rhyan Grant (36 derby appearances) says the rivalry is as fierce as ever.
Grant says the refreshed squad has good energy and the younger players are coachable.
No injury list or confirmed team news had been published when this was written.

fixtures.preview: A Sunday-afternoon home game, played as a doubleheader with the women's match against Melbourne City.

big_matches.title: Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain
big_matches.why: Heavyweights meet at the Etihad on matchday 2, with PSG as reigning champions.
talking_points: City arrive on a five-game winning run that includes a 3-0 win at Liverpool on 11 October; PSG have won three, drawn one and lost one of their last five.
Erling Haaland has 59 Champions League goals in 59 games, and one more equals Ruud van Nistelrooy's 60.
Haaland's fitness is being checked after he was substituted for Norway; City's update was due closer to kick-off.
